intent: Let a user turn one independent setting on or off, with the change taking effect immediately.
typical_uses: A setting that applies the moment it changes (notifications, dark mode, a feature flag)

dont_use_when.situation: An option that only takes effect once the surrounding form is submitted
Mutually exclusive choices, only one of which may be on
A pressed/unpressed button in a toolbar, drawn as a button rather than a track and knob

invariants.text: `checked` and `defaultChecked` are both accepted; `defaultChecked` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `checked` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a switch with no visible label and no aria-label
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pair it with `Label` for a shared click target, or pass `aria-label` directly when there is no visible text
Switch takes no content - wrap the switch and the label text together in `Label`, which is also what gives the pair one shared click target
A controlled switch with no change handler never receives its own toggle back - pair `checked` with `onCheckedChange`, or drop both and use `defaultChecked` for an uncontrolled switch

a11y.by: Base UI's own Switch primitive (role="switch", keyboard toggling, a hidden native input for form submission, data-checked/data-unchecked) plus switch.test.tsx's own role/aria-checked/data-checked assertions

onCheckedChange.states: onCheckedChange is a function called with the next checked value and event details, not a value
onCheckedChange.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its second argument carries Base UI's own change-event-details shape (a reason, the triggering native event, and controls to cancel the change or allow it to propagate), which only tsc can check.

inputRef.states: inputRef is a ref to the hidden native input Base UI renders for form submission
inputRef.because: `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - neither is expressible in JSON Schema. It exists so a consumer can read or focus the native input directly, the same input `name`/`value`/`uncheckedValue` submit through.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the switch's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the switch's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (checked, disabled, readOnly, required). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through switch.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: switch.tsx renders it directly inside its own Root wrapper as the knob that slides between the two ends of the track; it is not exported as a component of its own, so a consumer cannot reach or replace it independently - only the whole Switch.

good.title: Compact, unlabelled row named for assistive tech

bad.title: Label text passed as children
bad.why: Switch takes no content - there is no slot for it, and the text is silently dropped because the component's own Thumb always renders in its place. Wrap the switch and the text together in `Label` instead, which is also what gives the pair one shared click target.

bad.title: Controlled with no change handler
bad.why: `checked` with no `onCheckedChange` never gets its own toggle back, so the switch is stuck controlled and never responds to a click. Pair `checked` with `onCheckedChange`, or use `defaultChecked` instead.

Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc. inputRef is a ref to the hidden native input Base UI renders for form submission. `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - neither is expressible in JSON Schema. It exists so a consumer can read or focus the native input directly, the same input `name`/`value`/`uncheckedValue` submit through.

Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc. onCheckedChange is a function called with the next checked value and event details, not a value. A function type has no JSON Schema representation.
